deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the next folio): p prime, a has order α mod p (a^α ≡ 1), and b satisfies b^β ≡ a^γ (mod p). The context implies, though this page does not state it, that β is the least exponent with b^β in <a>. Then <a,b> is a cyclic subgroup of (Z/p)^* of order αβ, and its elements are a^x b^y with 0≤x<α, 0≤y<β. The page builds a generator of this subgroup, equivalently a β-th root of a.

(0) Top lines. The roots of x^λ ≡ a^γ inside <a> are listed as a^{γ'}, a^{γ'+α'}, a^{γ'+2α'}, ..., a^{γ'+(λ-1)α'}. Here α = λα' and γ = λγ' (my reading of the primes). These are the λ roots: one particular root times the λ-th roots of unity a^{kα'}. Then b^{β'} is written, followed by a partly illegible note.

(1) Since gcd(α,β,γ)=1 is needed for the next step, write αA + βB + γC = 1 with B, C > 0. Put c ≡ a^B b^C. Then c^β ≡ a^{βB} b^{βC} ≡ a^{βB} a^{γC} = a^{βB+γC}. My filled step: βB+γC = 1-αA and a^α ≡ 1, so c^β ≡ a.

(2) Claim: no power of c below the β-th is ≡ a. Gauss starts: if c^{β''} ≡ a with β''<β, then c^{β-β''} ≡ 1. The argument breaks off there.
- My completion: with C prime to β (noted at the bottom left, 'C primus ad β'), the image of c in <a,b>/<a> ≅ Z/β is b^C, which has order β. So c^k lies in <a> only if β | k.
- Hence ord(c) = β·ord(a) = αβ, so c generates <a,b>.

(3) Right margin, general criterion. c = a^x b^y (x<α) has full order αβ iff (i) y is prime to β, and (ii) βx+γy is prime to α. Reason: (i) makes the image in the quotient have order β, and c^β = a^{βx+γy} has order α iff (ii) holds.

(4) Bottom middle, case y=1, c = a^x b. Here c^0=1, c^1=a^x b and c^β = a^{βx+γ}, so the condition is gcd(βx+γ, α)=1. Writing αt + (βx+γ)u = 1, i.e. αt + β(xu) + γu = 1, and comparing with αA+βB+γC=1 gives C=u, B=xC, i.e. x = B/C (mod α). So the construction in (1) is recovered.

(5) Left table, numerical example α=36, β=20, γ=15 (the values used on the next folio). Gauss lists the powers of g = a^4 b^3: a^4b^3, a^8b^6, a^12b^9, a^16b^12, a^20b^15, a^24b^18. Then g^7 = a^28 b^21 = a^28·a^15·b = a^43 b = a^7 b, with the '21' noting the exponent of b. So g^7 = a^7 b, a generator of the form a^x b.
- Checks: for a^4b^3, βx+γy = 125 ≡ 17 (mod 36), prime to 36. For a^7 b, βx+γ = 155 ≡ 11 (mod 36), prime to 36.
- The side column '20 a^7 | a^11 b^3' is unclear. (a^7 b)^20 = a^11, and a^7·a^4b^3 = a^11 b^3.
- 'x=1' / '15' probably note that x=1 gives βx+γ = 35, prime to 36, so ab is a generator.
- The next folio counts all such (x,y) and gets 192 = φ(720).
errors: Exponent slip in the root list: 'a^{γ'+2α''}' should read a^{γ'+2α'}. The cancelled last exponent is corrected to γ'+(λ-1)α'.
The listed roots are only valid if λ | α and λ | γ (α=λα', γ=λγ'). This is implicit, not stated.
The step a^{βB+γC} ≡ a silently uses βB+γC = 1-αA and a^α ≡ 1.
Solvability of αA+βB+γC=1 needs gcd(α,β,γ)=1, which is not stated.
Claim (2) needs C prime to β (only noted separately at the bottom) and β minimal with b^β ∈ <a>. Without these the claim can fail.
In general αA+βB+γC=1 does not force gcd(C,β)=1, so that condition must be added, as Gauss does in the margin.

results.what: Roots of x^λ ≡ a^γ in the cyclic group <a>: a^{γ'+kα'}, k=0..λ-1, with α=λα', γ=λγ'
results.modern_name: Solving binomial congruences in a cyclic group (index calculus)

results.what: Construction of c = a^B b^C with c^β ≡ a from αA+βB+γC=1, giving a generator of <a,b> of order αβ
results.modern_name: Generator of a cyclic extension group / combining elements to raise multiplicative order (constructive primitive-root style argument)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones art. 55 ff. for combining elements of coprime orders)

results.what: a^x b^y has order αβ iff gcd(y,β)=1 and gcd(βx+γy,α)=1; worked example α=36, β=20, γ=15 with (a^4b^3)^7 = a^7 b
results.modern_name: Generator criterion for a cyclic group given as an extension of Z/α by Z/β (presentation a^α=1, b^β=a^γ)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard finite abelian group theory (19th century; Gauss, Schering, Kronecker)

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary computations on generators of a cyclic subgroup of (Z/p)^* given by a^α=1, b^β=a^γ, in the circle of ideas of Disquisitiones arts. 52-57 on primitive roots. The presentation by generator and relation is nice in an abelian-group spirit, but the content is routine for Gauss.

checkable.asserts: a^4 b^3 satisfies the generator criterion for α=36, β=20, γ=15.
a^7 b is a generator and (a^7 b)^20 = a^11.
x=1: a*b is a generator (βx+γ = 35 is prime to 36).

checkable.sympy: sum(1 for x in range(36) for y in range(20) if gcd(y,20)==1 and gcd(20*x+15*y,36)==1) == totient(720) == 192
checkable.asserts: The criterion picks out exactly φ(αβ) = 192 generators, matching the next folio.

checkable.sympy: all(((gcd(y,20)==1 and gcd(20*x+15*y,36)==1) == (gcd((20*x+15*y) % 720, 720)==1)) for x in range(36) for y in range(20))
checkable.asserts: In the additive model Z/720 with a=20 (order 36) and b=15 (20*b = 15*a), the criterion is equivalent to 20x+15y being a unit mod 720, i.e. a^x b^y generates.
Example of αA+βB+γC=1 (A=-1, B=1, C=1): c = a b has c^20 = a^{20+15} = a^{35+...}; βB+γC ≡ 1 (mod α) gives c^β = a.

transcription_corrections: 'a^{γ'+2α''}' on the page is a slip by Gauss for a^{γ'+2α'}.
The cancelled material in the last exponent is a struck-through 'αα'' replaced by '(λ-1)α'' written above.
'a.e.A' after b^{β'} is uncertain; it may be an abbreviation such as 'a. E. A.'. It is illegible as a formula.
The bottom-left entries '7 a^7 b' and '21' denote g^7 = a^7 b with the original b-exponent 21 = 7·3.
The right-margin note read as 'x = 1' is faint and uncertain.
Margin header: '43c/34' is struck through; the folio number is (43).
